subject: english-language
title: Fact or Fiction?
welcome_lead: Some texts make worlds; others report on the real one.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on fiction vs non-fiction reading.
final_note: You can now sort texts into fiction and non-fiction families.

concepts.def: Texts about real events or facts.
True story of part of a life.
Non-fiction piece in a paper or site.

walkthroughs.body_html: Fiction is made up; non-fiction is based on real events. Knowing which you're reading shapes how you judge truth.
Fiction comes in many forms: novel, short story, play, poem. Each has different length and shape.
Non-fiction includes articles, memoirs, biographies, reviews and reports. Each has its own conventions.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between transitive and intransitive verbs?
options: Transitive verbs are action verbs and intransitive are linking verbs.
Transitive verbs take a direct object ('she ate the cake'); intransitive verbs don't ('she slept'). Some verbs are both depending on use ('she ran' / 'she ran the company').
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Transitive verbs end in -ed and intransitive in -ing.

mcqs.q: What is the telegraphic stage of child language development?
options: Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.
It is the stage when children first start using a telephone.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Around age 2-3, children produce short utterances containing content words but omitting function words and inflections (e.g. 'mummy gone shop').

mcqs.q: What is an adjacency pair in conversation analysis?
options: It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Adjacency pairs are two people who sit next to each other while talking.
Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.
A two-part sequence where the first part conditions the second — question/answer, greeting/greeting, request/acceptance-or-refusal. The second part is 'conditionally relevant' on the first.
